title: Perfect annihilator for a map to a supported complex
statement: Let Y be quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-pc-scheme], let V be a quasi-compact open, and let T=Y\setminus V. For a morphism alpha:P\to Q in D_QCoh(Y) [def-pc-derived-category], assume either (i) P is perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex] and Q is supported on T, or (ii) P is pseudo-coherent [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex], Q is supported on T, and Q is bounded below. Then there is a morphism I\to\mathcal O_Y from a perfect complex I that is an isomorphism on V and for which I\otimes^L P\to Q, the composite of the tensor action with alpha, is zero.

proof.text: Use rhom_supported_quasiCoherent with the unchanged perfect/pseudo-coherent disjunction, converting the cohomological bound to IsGE via DerivedCategory.isGE_iff. Stalk vanishing of Q on V makes each restricted homology sheaf zero by section_ext. Apply the internal-Hom support clause to the closed complement of V; homology detects zero, so K=RHom(P,Q) is quasi-coherent and has zero derived restriction to V.

Apply scheme_derivedInternalHom_adjunction and transpose the map leftUnitor followed by alpha to a:unit → K. The tensor unit is perfect: at every point choose the top open and the single complex of the rank-one free module. Apply supported_perfect_factorization to a, obtaining unit → R → K with R perfect and zero on V. This proved helper realizes the original generator telescope, compact Hom, and finite thick factorization steps in D_QCoh(Y).

Complete unit → R to a distinguished triangle and inverse-rotate it to I → unit → R → I[1]. Two-out-of-three gives perfectness of I. Exact restriction maps this triangle to a distinguished triangle whose third vertex is zero, so its first arrow is invertible. The consecutive-composite equation and the factorization of a give i ≫ a = 0.

Specialize adjunction naturality to i in the first variable and identities in the other variables. This equates the adjunct of i ≫ a with i whiskered by P followed by the adjunct of a. The shared K-flat derived tensor is additive, using DerivedCategory.monoidalPreadditive with the same local sheaf tensor/closedness/flat-resolution instances used in schemeDerivedTensorMonoidal; hence its whiskering of zero is zero. Naturality with the zero source endomorphism proves that the adjunct of zero is zero even though the adjunction interface is only an Equiv. The inverse-equivalence equation identifies the adjunct of a with leftUnitor followed by alpha, giving exactly the unchanged conclusion.

lean.statement: theorem exists_perfect_annihilator (Y : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace Y] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y] (V : Y.Opens) [CompactSpace (V : Set Y)] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))] [∀ U : Y.Opens, HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace).over U))] (P Q : schemeDerivedQCohCategory Y) (α : P ⟶ Q) (hcase : Scheme.IsPerfect Y P.obj ∨ Scheme.IsPseudoCoherent Y P.obj ∧ ∃ n : ℤ, ∀ k : ℤ, k < n → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) k).obj Q.obj)) (hQ : ∀ (k : ℤ) (x : Y), x ∈ V → Subsingleton (↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) k).obj Q.obj).val.presheaf x))) : ∃ (I : schemeDerivedCategory Y) (i : I ⟶ 𝟙_ (schemeDerivedCategory Y)), Scheme.IsPerfect Y I ∧ IsIso ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace) V).mapDerivedCategory.map i) ∧ i ▷ P.obj ≫ (λ_ P.obj).hom ≫ α.hom = 0
